spec.title: Example 286's adversarial fixture on 5.3.19: a setter that writes the protected flag is told from its honest twin, by its effect contract and through the binder
spec.description: The state stream of the domain-advances brief, step 5. Example 286's frozen protected-state claim binds onto ProtectedBean, whose setters are all honest, so it cannot tell the binder's guarantee (about field names) from the bean's. proofs/beans/ adds an account whose admin flag is protected by the disallowed pattern "admin": AccountBean, whose permitted setName also sets admin when the name starts "admin:", its honest twin HonestAccountBean, the entry AccountBinding (DataBinder.bind of one value {field, value} onto a fresh account, then its admin flag), and AccountBeanStandIn, the bean wrapper's write on these two beans, sampled against 5.3.19's method before each run (462,336 samples, all equal). proofs/beans.py runs five checks at bound 8 on 5.3.19: the setter's effect contract (--writes this.name, this.name == name) refuted on AccountBean and established on HonestAccountBean; the application-level statement !result refuted on AccountBean through an allowed field name, its witness run on a JVM; established on the twin through the honest setter's effect contract, which stands in for the setter call the stand-in makes; and refused with the adversarial setter's contract, which is refuted. Each was run inline as a capped probe in about a minute and gave its expected answer. None of these files is in target.json's adapter set or under proofs/stand-ins, so the accepted refutation of vulnerable-protected-state-mutation is unaffected.
